# GitHub PR Review

## Overview

Technical mechanics for GitHub PR review workflows via `gh` CLI. Covers fetching review comments, replying to threads, creating/updating PRs.

**Companion skill:** For *how to evaluate* feedback, see `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. This skill covers *how to interact* with GitHub.

**Security:** Use fine-grained PAT with minimal permissions.

## Setup (One-Time)

### Fine-Grained PAT

Create at github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Fine-grained tokens:

| Permission | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Pull requests | Read & Write |
| Contents | Read |

**Can't:** Delete repos, push code, delete branches, manage settings.

### Configure & Allowlist

```bash
export GH_TOKEN="github_pat_xxxx"
```

Add to `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(gh repo view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr ready:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr edit:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments/*/replies:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Quick Reference

| Operation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| Get owner/repo | `gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"'` |
| Get PR number | `gh pr view --json number -q .number` |
| Get PR author | `gh pr view --json author -q .author.login` |
| Fetch all review comments | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments --paginate` |
| Get single comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}` |
| Reply to comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="msg"` |
| Create PR | `gh pr create --title "T" --body "B" [--draft]` |
| Mark ready | `gh pr ready [number]` |
| Convert to draft | `gh pr ready --undo [number]` |
| Edit PR | `gh pr edit [number] --title "T" --body "B"` |

## Workflow: Respond to PR Review

### 1. Get repo info and PR details

```bash
owner_repo=$(gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"')
pr_number=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number)
pr_author=$(gh pr view --json author -q .author.login)
```

### 2. Fetch and analyze threads

```bash
# Fetch all comments and group into threads, showing last author per thread
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq 'sort_by([.in_reply_to_id // .id, .created_at]) | group_by(.in_reply_to_id // .id) | map({thread_id: (.[0].in_reply_to_id // .[0].id), path: .[0].path, line: (.[0].line // .[0].original_line), last_author: .[-1].user.login, last_body: .[-1].body[0:100], count: length})'
```

### 3. Filter to threads needing response

```bash
# Filter to threads where last_author != PR author
# Note: Use '| not' instead of '!=' to avoid shell escaping issues with !
... | jq --arg author "$pr_author" '[.[] | select(.last_author == $author | not)]'
```

For each thread needing response:
- Read the comment + file/line context
- Apply `superpowers:receiving-code-review` skill for evaluation
- Fix code and/or reply to thread

### 4. Commit fixes and push
- run the build, tests, linting as required
- commit the changes, noting the commit sha
- push the changes so they're visible
- We need to do this FIRST so we have the commit shas to put into the replies to the pr review

### 5. Re-fetch comment IDs (if rebased)

**Important:** If you rebased or force-pushed, comment IDs may have changed. Re-fetch the comment threads before replying:

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq '...'
```

### 6. Reply to a thread

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies \
  -f body="Fixed in commit abc123. [description of fix]"
```

### 7. Summarize and finish

After all threads addressed, ask if ready to mark PR ready for review.

**Note:** REST API doesn't expose "resolved" status. We infer "done" when PR author made last comment in thread.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Broad PAT permissions | Use fine-grained PAT with only Pull requests + Contents |
| Missing pagination | Always use `--paginate` for comment fetching |
| Top-level reply | Use `/comments/{id}/replies` endpoint, not `/comments` |
| Re-responding to threads | Skip threads where PR author made last comment |
| Forgetting to reply after fix | Always reply to confirm the fix was made |
| jq `!=` fails with shell error | Use `select(.x == "y" \| not)` instead of `select(.x != "y")` |
| 404 on reply after rebase | Comment IDs change after force-push/rebase. Re-fetch comments before replying |

4. But the shadow branch is still named with the **old** BaseCommit hash

1. `ActionCondense` case (line 585-589): `condenseAndUpdateState` returns `false` → `condensed` stays `false`
2. Line 621: `!condensed && !hasPendingMigration` → `true` 
3. `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` updates `state.BaseCommit` to `newHead`
4. Line 626: State is saved with the new BaseCommit

# GitHub PR Review

## Overview

Technical mechanics for GitHub PR review workflows via `gh` CLI. Covers fetching review comments, replying to threads, creating/updating PRs.

**Companion skill:** For *how to evaluate* feedback, see `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. This skill covers *how to interact* with GitHub.

**Security:** Use fine-grained PAT with minimal permissions.

## Setup (One-Time)

### Fine-Grained PAT

Create at github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Fine-grained tokens:

| Permission | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Pull requests | Read & Write |
| Contents | Read |

**Can't:** Delete repos, push code, delete branches, manage settings.

### Configure & Allowlist

```bash
export GH_TOKEN="github_pat_xxxx"
```

Add to `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(gh repo view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr ready:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr edit:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments/*/replies:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Quick Reference

| Operation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| Get owner/repo | `gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"'` |
| Get PR number | `gh pr view --json number -q .number` |
| Get PR author | `gh pr view --json author -q .author.login` |
| Fetch all review comments | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments --paginate` |
| Get single comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}` |
| Reply to comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="msg"` |
| Create PR | `gh pr create --title "T" --body "B" [--draft]` |
| Mark ready | `gh pr ready [number]` |
| Convert to draft | `gh pr ready --undo [number]` |
| Edit PR | `gh pr edit [number] --title "T" --body "B"` |

## Workflow: Respond to PR Review

### 1. Get repo info and PR details

```bash
owner_repo=$(gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"')
pr_number=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number)
pr_author=$(gh pr view --json author -q .author.login)
```

### 2. Fetch and analyze threads

```bash
# Fetch all comments and group into threads, showing last author per thread
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq 'sort_by([.in_reply_to_id // .id, .created_at]) | group_by(.in_reply_to_id // .id) | map({thread_id: (.[0].in_reply_to_id // .[0].id), path: .[0].path, line: (.[0].line // .[0].original_line), last_author: .[-1].user.login, last_body: .[-1].body[0:100], count: length})'
```

### 3. Filter to threads needing response

```bash
# Filter to threads where last_author != PR author
# Note: Use '| not' instead of '!=' to avoid shell escaping issues with !
... | jq --arg author "$pr_author" '[.[] | select(.last_author == $author | not)]'
```

For each thread needing response:
- Read the comment + file/line context
- Apply `superpowers:receiving-code-review` skill for evaluation
- Fix code and/or reply to thread

### 4. Commit fixes and push
- run the build, tests, linting as required
- commit the changes, noting the commit sha
- push the changes so they're visible
- We need to do this FIRST so we have the commit shas to put into the replies to the pr review

### 5. Re-fetch comment IDs (if rebased)

**Important:** If you rebased or force-pushed, comment IDs may have changed. Re-fetch the comment threads before replying:

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq '...'
```

### 6. Reply to a thread

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies \
  -f body="Fixed in commit abc123. [description of fix]"
```

### 7. Summarize and finish

After all threads addressed, ask if ready to mark PR ready for review.

**Note:** REST API doesn't expose "resolved" status. We infer "done" when PR author made last comment in thread.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Broad PAT permissions | Use fine-grained PAT with only Pull requests + Contents |
| Missing pagination | Always use `--paginate` for comment fetching |
| Top-level reply | Use `/comments/{id}/replies` endpoint, not `/comments` |
| Re-responding to threads | Skip threads where PR author made last comment |
| Forgetting to reply after fix | Always reply to confirm the fix was made |
| jq `!=` fails with shell error | Use `select(.x == "y" \| not)` instead of `select(.x != "y")` |
| 404 on reply after rebase | Comment IDs change after force-push/rebase. Re-fetch comments before replying |

Yeah, there are two specific risks:

1. **Silent drop in `ApplyCommonActions`**: The switch at line 304 has no `default` case. A new action that isn't listed in either the common or strategy-specific arms just... vanishes. No error, no log.

2. **Silent drop in callers**: PostCommit's dispatch loop also has no `default`. If a new strategy-specific action gets added to the passthrough list at line 310-311 but PostCommit doesn't add a `case` for it, same thing — silently ignored.

The root issue is that `Action` is an `int` iota, so Go won't give us exhaustive switch checking. A few options:

**Option A — `default: panic/log.Fatal`**: Add `default` arms to both `ApplyCommonActions` and PostCommit's loop that panic or `log.Fatal` on unknown actions. Turns silent drops into loud failures during development. Downside: panics in production git hooks are bad.

**Option B — Validation function**: Add an `AllActions()` or `ValidateActionHandling()` function that returns the full set, and write a unit test asserting that every action is covered by both `ApplyCommonActions` and PostCommit. If someone adds an action and forgets a handler, the test fails. This is the test-as-documentation approach.

**Option C — Typed dispatch (heavier)**: Replace the `[]Action` return with a struct like `PostCommitActions { Condense bool; Migrate bool; ... }`. Compiler enforces field access. But this couples the state machine to strategy concerns.

I'd lean toward **B** — a test that iterates all action constants and asserts coverage. It's lightweight, catches the exact failure mode we're worried about, and doesn't risk panics in user git hooks. Want to go that direction, or do you have a different instinct?

**Option A: Struct of funcs (handler table)**

```go
type ActionHandlers struct {
    Condense              func(*State) error
    CondenseIfFilesTouched func(*State) error
    DiscardIfNoFiles       func(*State) error
    MigrateShadowBranch   func(*State) error
    WarnStaleSession       func(*State) error

func ApplyTransition(state *State, result TransitionResult, h ActionHandlers) error {
    // framework applies common effects, then dispatches strategy actions
    // via h.Condense(state), h.MigrateShadowBranch(state), etc.
}
```

No-ops are inline: `WarnStaleSession: func(*State) error { return nil }`. Adding a new field leaves it `nil` at construction sites, so you'd need a `Validate()` that checks all fields are non-nil — runtime, but fails at init time, not deep in a git hook. Less ceremony than a full interface, but the safety is runtime not compile-time.

**Option B: Collapse strategy actions to a single enum**

Looking at the actual transitions, every phase+event combo produces *at most one* strategy-specific action. The `[]Action` slice mixes common effects with strategy actions, which is what creates the dispatch problem. Separate them:

```go
type TransitionResult struct {
    NewPhase        Phase
    CommonEffects   CommonEffects      // bitmask: UpdateInteraction | ClearEndedAt
    StrategyAction  StrategyAction     // single value, not a slice
}
```

`ApplyTransition` handles common effects internally and returns the single `StrategyAction` for the caller. Simpler to reason about, but same exhaustiveness gap as today — Go won't enforce the switch.

input.description:
## Problem

The state machine in `session/phase.go` returns `[]Action` from `ApplyCommonActions`, and callers (e.g., `PostCommit` in `manual_commit_hooks.go`) must dispatch each action in a `switch`. This pattern has two silent-drop risks:

1. **Framework gap**: `ApplyCommonActions` (line 299) routes actions to either "apply internally" or "pass through as `remaining`". Its switch has no `default` — a new action not listed in either arm silently vanishes before the caller ever sees it.

2. **Caller gap**: The caller's dispatch loop also has no exhaustiveness guarantee. Go's `exhaustive` linter (already enabled) catches missing `case` arms, but only if the action reaches the caller in the first place (see #1).

Adding a new `Action` constant requires updating **both** the framework routing and every caller's switch. There's no compile-time enforcement — you discover the miss at runtime (or never, if it's a silent no-op).

This was surfaced during PR #172 review while fixing a condensation-failure bug in the PostCommit dispatch loop.

## Proposed Solution: `ActionHandler` interface

Invert control so the framework **calls the caller** instead of returning a bag of actions:

```go
// ActionHandler defines strategy-specific side effects for state transitions.
// The framework calls these during ApplyTransition — the compiler enforces
// that every strategy-specific action has a handler.
type ActionHandler interface {
    HandleCondense(state *State) error
    HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched(state *State) error
    HandleDiscardIfNoFiles(state *State) error
    HandleMigrateShadowBranch(state *State) error
    HandleWarnStaleSession(state *State) error
}
```

Replace `ApplyCommonActions` with `ApplyTransition`:

```go
func ApplyTransition(state *State, result TransitionResult, handler ActionHandler) error {
    state.Phase = result.NewPhase
    for _, action := range result.Actions {
        switch action {
        case ActionUpdateLastInteraction:
            now := time.Now()
            state.LastInteractionTime = &now
        case ActionClearEndedAt:
            state.EndedAt = nil
        case ActionCondense:
            if err := handler.HandleCondense(state); err != nil { return err }
        case ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched:
            if err := handler.HandleCondenseIfFilesTouched(state); err != nil { return err }
        // ... remaining strategy-specific actions
        }
    }
    return nil
}
```

Callers construct a handler struct that captures per-invocation context:

```go
type postCommitActionHandler struct {
    s                      *ManualCommitStrategy
    logCtx                 context.Context
    repo                   *git.Repository
    checkpointID           string
    // ... other per-call context
}

func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleCondense(state *State) error { /* ... */ }
func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleWarnStaleSession(state *State) error { return nil } // explicit no-op
```

**Key benefit**: Add a new `Action` → add a method to `ActionHandler` → compiler error at every callsite that doesn't implement it.

## Alternatives Considered

| Approach | Compile-time safe? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Interface** (proposed) | Yes | Most Go-idiomatic for this; small interface (5 methods) |
| **`exhaustive` linter** | Partially | Already enabled; catches caller switches but NOT the framework's routing gap in `ApplyCommonActions` |
| **Struct of func fields** | No (runtime) | Less ceremony but nil-field checks are runtime only |
| **Single strategy action enum** | No | Each transition has ≤1 strategy action, but still no switch exhaustiveness |

## Scope

- Introduce `ActionHandler` interface in `session/phase.go`
- Replace `ApplyCommonActions` → `ApplyTransition` (framework calls handler methods)
- Refactor `PostCommit` dispatch loop in `manual_commit_hooks.go` to use handler struct
- Update any other callers of `ApplyCommonActions`
- Existing tests should continue passing (behavior unchanged)

## Context

- PR #172: Phase-aware PostCommit (where this was identified)
- Commits `eafc951` and `9e64962`: Fixed the immediate bug (condensation failure orphaning shadow branches) and added test coverage for the dispatch loop
- The dispatch loop now has comprehensive tests (7 new cases), so this refactor has a safety net

## Problem

Gemini's `handleGeminiAfterAgent` in `hooks_geminicli_handlers.go` doesn't use the session state machine for turn-end transitions. Unlike Claude Code's handler which calls `transitionSessionTurnEnd()` → `session.Transition(EventTurnEnd)`, Gemini goes straight to `commitGeminiSession()` without firing `EventTurnEnd`.

This means:
- Phase transitions on turn end (ACTIVE → IDLE, ACTIVE_COMMITTED → IDLE) don't fire for Gemini sessions
- Deferred condensation (ACTIVE_COMMITTED → IDLE emitting `ActionCondense`) won't work for Gemini
- Session phase tracking is incomplete for Gemini agents

## Context

- Claude Code's `transitionSessionTurnEnd` was wired up in the ENT-221 PR stack (#168-#174)
- A bug was found where `transitionSessionTurnEnd` ignores `ActionCondense` from `ApplyCommonActions` return value — fixing that in PR #172
- Once that fix lands, Gemini should adopt the same pattern

## Scope

- Add `EventTurnEnd` transition to Gemini's `handleGeminiAfterAgent`
- Dispatch strategy-specific actions from the transition (particularly `ActionCondense`)
- Ensure parity with Claude Code's turn-end handling
- Add test coverage
